# Ñāṇakathā (Ps 1.1)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ñāṇakathā* ("Discussion of Knowledge") constitutes the opening treatise of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Hazra 1994]. The text begins with a table of contents (*mātikā*) that lists seventy-three knowledges; this matrix specifically details the contents of the *Ñāṇakathā* rather than the whole of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Norman 1983; Hazra 1994]. Although it retains canonical sutta formulas such as *evaṁ me sutaṁ* and the vocative *bhikkhave*, its format—systematically resolving topics through questions and answers—closely reflects the method of the Abhidhamma [Norman 1983]. The treatise details doctrines of wisdom and insight, including knowledge of the impermanence and unsatisfactoriness of conditioned formations, the four noble truths, dependent origination, and systems of insight knowledges and eighteen great insights (*mahāvipassanā*) [Hazra 1994; Buddhist Forum v4]. It also provides a foundational canonical definition of the Buddha's omniscience (*sabbaññutañāṇa*), specifying that the Tathāgata knows everything conditioned and unconditioned without remainder across the past, present, and future [Pandey 1972; Jayatilleke 1963].

  In addition, DharmaNexus aligns the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan technical works, showing notable matches with the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and its *Nibandhana*, the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya*, the *Mahāvyutpatti*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and various *Prajñāpāramitā* texts [DharmaNexus].
